stories.title: Beast of Burden
stories.fortuneLine: Praise will set a tower on your spine, and the twenty-sixth life is the bridle.
stories.body:
This happened in the 25th rebirth of the universe. The stars were young again, and the wolf still remembered being hungry.

He found a donkey in a valley of sleep, and whispered: “The world needs your strength. I will build something great, but only with your help.” The donkey, flattered, agreed.

Each day he carried stone, dragged iron, bled his hooves. “A temple,” said the wolf. “A monument,” said the wolf. “A promise to the light.” And the donkey labored while the wolf smiled and sharpened his teeth.

When the tower touched the sky, the wolf climbed to its peak, opened his jaws, and swallowed the sun. Darkness fell. And still the donkey stood below, waiting for thanks.

He did not understand. But the owls did. And the mice. And the wind.

The universe was born again, and again. And in the 26th rebirth, the watchers gave the wolf a limp. And gave the donkey no sympathy. They made him a servant to man for his stupidity.

And to this day, the wolf still looks up at the sun, his belly cold with longing.
